regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, author block, and ESI/CCDC footnote
regions.finding: Article identity and aggregate Fe-catalyzed inversion claim were inspected. The page states ESI availability, but workspace mapping leaves SI association unestablished; no SI fact was imported. CCDC 940135 is a crystallographic deposition, not an associated SI file.
Generic inversion/retention drawing with R groups and LG is classified as a general scheme, not an experiment-specific preparation.

Equation (1) is explicitly previous Nelson work and is retained as a literature example with 79–94% product 2 and 0–6% product 3. Equation (2) is the generic current Fe coupling and is classified as a general scheme; row-level current experiments are Tables 1–4 and Equation (3).
Narrative values for Fe(acac)3/THF and alternative solvents/catalysts map to Table 1 entries on page 2 and were linked rather than duplicated.

unresolved: Generic schemes do not define full structures or complete procedures.
The ESI is mentioned by the paper but no supplied file is explicitly associated.

regions.finding: Ten distinct catalyst/solvent optimization or control rows were retained with shared substrate/MeMgCl/solvent quantities, row catalyst/loading/time, NMR yield, 3a/2a marker, entry-8 2a yield, and entry-9/10 recoveries. Dashes remain source markers; no-iron and CuCl controls are independent rows.
ORTEP is characterization of 3a and not a second preparation. It supports the Table 2 entry-3 product assignment without verifying the candidate SMILES.

Eleven racemic substrate-scope rows were retained independently with shared FeCl3·6H2O/THF conditions and row scale/time/silyl overrides, yields, product labels, and 3/2 ratios. Entry 3 is the same experiment as the page-4 typical procedure and is merged with that evidence.
Eight optically active substrate rows were retained independently with starting ee, product configuration/yield/ee, 3/2 ratio, entry-3 2 h override, and entry-7/8 TBS plus 4 mmol override.

unresolved: Most table rows omit atmosphere, workup, purification, isolated masses, and analytical bases.
Complex stereochemical candidates remain unverified and stereochemistry is retained chiefly in labels.

regions.finding: Six independent alkyl-Grignard rows were retained. Entry 1 is a complex-mixture failure; rows 2–6 preserve catalyst/solvent/additive changes, NaI and H2O quantities from the footnote, scale overrides, isolated yields, and 3/2 ratios.
A separate enantioenriched (R)-1b experiment with n-BuMgCl, Fe(acac)3, NaI, H2O, and Et2O gives (S)-3n in 68% yield/98% ee and 94/6 ratio by NMR. It is not merged with racemic Table 4 entry 5.
The Lewis-acid-mediated SN2/Walden-inversion drawing is a proposed mechanism. Its organometallic and Lewis-acid species are explicitly unresolved and were not represented as isolated experiments.

The prose introduces benzyl ester formation, desilylation, and stereodivergent terminal-alkyne allenylation; the actual six arrows and conditions are on page 4 and were linked cross-page rather than duplicated.

unresolved: Table 4 and Equation (3) omit several operational and analytical details.
The real in-situ iron/magnesium species and role of water/NaI remain unclear in the source.

regions.finding: Two enantiomer-specific benzyl esterifications and four distinct R/S-diphenylprolinol allenylations were retained as six experiments. Each arrow's yield and final ee are product-specific; the detailed (Sa,2S,3S)-5 procedure is merged with its Scheme arrow.

One sequential desilylation/Sonogashira experiment was retained with TBAF, PhI, Pd(PPh3)2Cl2, CuI, Et3N, DMSO, staged conditions, 88% two-step yield, and 98% ee. The desilylation-stage yield remains unknown.

The exact 1 mmol 1a/MeMgCl typical procedure enriches Table 2 entry 3 with quantities, N2, addition time, -78 °C/1 h, quench/workup, chromatography, 167.3 mg/84% isolated 3a, crude-NMR 98/2 ratio, and melting point.

The detailed two-stage (2S,3R)-4m to (Sa,2S,3S)-5 experiment was merged with its Scheme 3 arrow. Exact stage-1 quantities/workup and stage-2 quantities/operations were structured. The original image prints ZnBr2 as 90.3 g and 0.40 mmol; this internal conflict is preserved for review rather than silently corrected.

unresolved: ZnBr2 is printed as 90.3 g for 0.40 mmol, a likely source unit error.
Three Scheme 3 allenylations lack detailed scale/workup/mass data on the inspected pages.

regions.region: page 5 upper-left continuation of (Sa,2S,3S)-5 procedure and characterization
regions.finding: Completes the existing detailed allenylation: silica-pad workup, chromatography, 88.5 mg, 57% isolated yield, and 99% ee with OJ-H HPLC conditions. Spectroscopy is characterization, not a second preparation.

Qiong Yu is thanked for reproducing preparations of 3d, (2S,3R)-3l, and 3o. No independent conditions, quantities, outcomes, or run identifiers are supplied, so no duplicate experiments were created; notes were linked to the corresponding Table 2/3/4 records.
Bibliography and prior-literature context only. External papers were not expanded into current-paper experiments.
